title: Foundations for everyday decisions.
description: Choose text by its job, color by its meaning, and spacing by the relationship between things. These guides use the existing Parya values from Paper.

typography.label: Page title
typography.use: Name the current page: Vendors, Bookings or Customers.
typography.avoid: A title inside a card or a large promotional slogan.

typography.label: Record title
typography.use: Name one open record, such as a booking, customer or vendor.
typography.avoid: Repeating the record name above every section.

typography.label: Dialog title
typography.use: Name the task in a dialog. Keep the title short and specific.
typography.avoid: Long instructions; put them in the description.

typography.label: Section title
typography.use: Start a main section within a page or form.
typography.avoid: A field label or ordinary paragraph.

typography.label: Subsection title
typography.use: Introduce a group inside a larger section.
typography.avoid: Skipping heading levels to make text smaller.

typography.label: Body
typography.example: Confirm the traveler’s passport name before issuing the ticket.
typography.use: Default reading text, instructions, policies and explanations.
typography.avoid: Shrinking important information into a caption.

typography.label: Body emphasis
typography.use: Emphasize a short important phrase within reading text.
typography.avoid: Making an entire paragraph semibold.

typography.label: Compact body
typography.use: Short table and list content where space is limited.
typography.avoid: Long policies, dense instructions or critical terms.

typography.label: Field label
typography.use: A visible name for a form field. TextField supplies the label association for you.
typography.avoid: Placeholder text as the only label.

typography.label: Action label
typography.use: A short verb describing the result of an action. Button applies its size-specific style.
typography.avoid: Styling a paragraph to look clickable without a real button.

typography.label: Tab label
typography.use: Switch between related views. Tabs use 500; the active tab uses 600.
typography.avoid: A page title or replacing tab semantics with plain text.

typography.label: Navigation label
typography.use: Name a destination. Navigation uses 500; the active destination uses 600.
typography.avoid: A lengthy description or instructions.

typography.label: Table heading
typography.use: Name a column with a real th element and the appropriate scope.
typography.avoid: Putting h2 or h3 elements inside table headers.

typography.label: Metadata
typography.use: Short supporting facts such as location, author or update time.
typography.avoid: Essential payment or cancellation instructions.

typography.label: Caption
typography.use: A short supporting note close to the related content.
typography.avoid: The only place a user can find a requirement or warning.

typography.label: Overline
typography.use: A short category marker in a dense operational view; use sparingly.
typography.avoid: Long text, repeated all-caps labels or required instructions.

typography.label: Reference
typography.use: Booking and document references that users scan or copy.
typography.avoid: Body paragraphs or all navigation labels.

typography.label: Date
typography.use: Compact dates in tables and schedules. Use DateText or a time element with a machine-readable date.
typography.avoid: Ambiguous dates without enough context.

typography.label: Money
typography.use: Comparable amounts in tables, totals and financial summaries. Money supplies locale-aware formatting.
typography.avoid: Rounding or calculating booking prices in presentation code.

typography.label: Count
typography.use: Tiny supporting counts in badges, with the meaning available in nearby text or an accessible name.
typography.avoid: A critical value with no readable label.

weights.name: Regular
weights.use: Paragraphs, instructions and supporting text. Start here for reading.

weights.name: Medium
weights.use: Navigation, inactive tabs and mono references. Adds structure without making everything bold.

weights.name: Semibold
weights.use: Actions, field labels, active navigation and short emphasis. Use selectively.

weights.name: Bold
weights.use: Page, record, dialog and section titles. Establish hierarchy rather than emphasizing whole paragraphs.

fonts.name: Onest
fonts.use: Headings, record names, prominent values and action labels.

fonts.name: Public Sans
fonts.use: Body text, forms, navigation and everyday operational reading.
fonts.example: Confirm the details before issuing tickets.

fonts.name: JetBrains Mono
fonts.use: References, dates and aligned amounts. Use sparingly outside data.

colorPairs.label: Surface
colorPairs.use: The main reading and working surface.

colorPairs.label: Supporting text
colorPairs.use: Descriptions that support the primary content.

colorPairs.label: Hints and metadata
colorPairs.use: Secondary facts that still need to be readable; never reduce opacity to make them quieter.

colorPairs.label: Primary action
colorPairs.use: Teal identifies the main action, such as Create booking.

colorPairs.label: Selected item
colorPairs.use: Pink identifies selection. Pair color with a check, border, or selected state.

colorPairs.label: Text link
colorPairs.use: Use an actual link for navigation and an underline in reading text.

colorPairs.label: Success
colorPairs.use: A completed or confirmed outcome; add a status label.

colorPairs.label: Warning
colorPairs.use: Something needs attention; explain what to do next.

colorPairs.label: Error or danger
colorPairs.use: An error or destructive action; name the issue and recovery.

colorPairs.label: Information
colorPairs.use: Context or a neutral update; include clear text.

principles.title: Choose a role first
principles.text: Use a named typography role or component instead of choosing an unrelated size and weight for each screen.

principles.title: Keep meaning in HTML
principles.text: Use one descriptive h1 for the page, h2 for its sections and h3 for subsections. A visual style does not determine the heading level.

principles.title: Make important text readable
principles.text: Use body text for policies, amounts due and instructions. Parya’s 10.5–12px dense-data roles are not a good default for essential reading.

principles.title: Support zoom and text spacing
principles.text: Allow text to wrap and containers to grow. Check text resized to 200% and user spacing overrides; do not fix a text block’s height to its default appearance.

principles.title: Use more than color
principles.text: Keep a visible status label, error message or selection marker. Color alone must not carry the meaning.
